title.narrative: Assessing the Feasibility of a UNESCO Qualifications Passport-Based Recognition Pathway for Rohingya Learners in Cox’s Bazar

description.narrative:
Education pathways for Rohingya learners remain structurally incomplete. The learners may study under the Myanmar Curriculum, but they do not yet have a sufficiently recognized, portable or externally meaningful record of learning achievement. This absence is especially problematic at secondary levels, where learners and families are more likely to question the value of continued education if completion does not lead to recognized progression. This weakens motivation and may contribute to dropout, child labour, early marriage, recruitment risks and other negative coping strategies, with the greatest effects likely to fall on children and adolescents already facing heightened barriers to participation, protection and progression.
The objective of the study is to determine the technical, institutional, operational and protection feasibility of applying or adapting the UNESCO Qualifications Passport (UQP) methodology to recognize Rohingya learners’ achievement under the Myanmar Curriculum.
